audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize a temporary tariff-margin windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filing attributes the 200-basis-point FY2025 gross-margin increase primarily to tariff timing
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary gross profit raises FY2025 OE and the fitted trend used for the $200 million anchor, increasing operating PV in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect gross margin to decrease as we start to recognize these higher tariff costs in our Statement of Operations and Comprehensive Income in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing distortion is demonstrated: prices rose before tariff-loaded inventory reached cost of goods sold, and higher costs began entering earnings in 2026. The filing does not isolate the FY2025 benefit, while subsequent $98.1 million tariff refunds further complicate normalization. Because the distortion affects the anchor applied across all forecast years, it is reasonably capable of materially changing value despite the haircut from $268.9 million to $200 million.
audit_findings.action: Match tariff-related price increases, inventory-layer costs, and refunds by period; exclude refund interest and other nonrecurring effects; rebuild normalized FY2025 OE and rerun the log-trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may omit a structurally large working-capital requirement
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified normalized requirement; FY2025 inventory cash use was $250.373 million, while $1,093.1 million of additional receivables would have existed without factoring; inventory released $150.488 million in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncharged recurring inventory and receivables funding would reduce distributable OE or increase forecast reinvestment required to support growth.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, cash provided by operating activities decreased $117.4 million from the prior year primarily as a result of cash used to fund investments in inventory to meet customer demand and to pay for increased tariffs on imports, partially offset by higher proceeds from selling accounts receivable under our customer-sponsored accounts receivable sales programs.
audit_findings.explanation: An omission is not demonstrated because much of the FY2025 inventory build reversed in 2026 and the 22% RONTA mechanism may already capture normalized reinvestment. Nevertheless, the filed working-capital movements are larger than the $200 million OE anchor, and receivables factoring displaces more than $1 billion of balance-sheet funding. Even a modest permanent component could materially reduce value, so double counting or omission must be resolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE, operating cash flow, inventory, receivables sold, factoring costs, and payables over a complete inventory cycle; calculate normalized working capital per dollar of organic sales and rerun the valuation with that requirement charged exactly once.

audit_findings.title: Supplier-investment income may be double counted with the $17.3 million stake bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed FY2025 investment income of $4.1 million and bridge value of $17.3 million; capitalizing the full $4.1 million at the supplied scenario PV-to-anchor multiples gives a conservative computed range of $48.8-$68.0 million, or $1.61-$2.25 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If investment income remains in OE while the related stakes are added separately, both the income stream and the assets producing it enter equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: These investments provided $ 4.1 million, $ 5.3 million, and $ 5.7 million of income during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The duplication itself is unresolved because the OE worksheet is not supplied. However, even treating the full pretax $4.1 million as recurring equity OE produces an upper-bound proxy of about 2% of scenario equity value and $2.25 per share, versus the $16.69 per-share gap between the bull value and market price. The $17.3 million bridge alone is only $0.57 per share. On the filed scale, this cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace equity-method and cost-method income through every OE year and document its tax treatment. Remove it from OE if included, or remove the associated stake bridge, and substantiate the bridge's realizable value.

audit_findings.title: Adding back the Heavy Duty impairment may conceal recurring acquisition capital destruction
audit_findings.magnitude: $56.706 million FY2025 impairment, equal to 28.4% of the $200 million anchor; any recurring acquisition-capital requirement is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back the impairment raises OE; value is overstated if forecast growth includes acquired earnings without charging the recurring cash cost of acquisitions and failed investments.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, we recorded an impairment charge of $ 56.7 million, representing the balance of goodwill in our Heavy Duty reporting unit as of the measurement date.
audit_findings.explanation: The impairment and apparent noncash addback are historical, but an impairment is a sunk accounting charge and its addback is not inherently an OE error. The potential error depends on whether the 0%-6% forecast growth requires continuing acquisitions or whether acquisition losses recur. The company calls acquisitions a key growth component, but the record does not allocate forecast growth between organic and acquired sources or establish a recurring loss rate, so materiality remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE impairment adjustment and compile acquisition cash spending, acquired OE, organic growth, and later impairments by acquisition cohort. If forecast growth requires acquisitions, rerun with the associated purchase investment and normalized failure cost.

audit_findings.title: Customer-credit estimates could materially overstate normalized revenue
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified potential under-accrual; filed year-end reserve was $197.398 million, with FY2025 provision of $404.198 million and charge-offs of $411.155 million
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated credit and return accrual inflates net revenue, profit, OE, and the trend anchor without creating a separately deducted bridge liability.
audit_findings.evidence: Subjective auditor judgment was required to evaluate the Company’s determination of the impact of market conditions on the length of time between when a sale occurs and a credit is issued for defective product returns.
audit_findings.explanation: No under-accrual is demonstrated. The filing states that actual credits historically did not differ materially from estimates, and the auditor tested post-year-end credits and relevant controls. Nevertheless, the reserve is nearly as large as the $200 million anchor, annual reserve activity exceeds twice the anchor, and two customers represent 40% of sales. The record provides no quantified estimation error or sensitivity, so it cannot establish whether the remaining valuation exposure is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the customer-credit reserve by category and major customer, compare post-year-end credits and returns with the FY2025 estimate, analyze reserve-to-sales and utilization trends, and rerun normalized revenue and OE for any identified under-accrual or changed customer terms.
